# Substack

> Substack is a media platform where writers, podcasters, video creators, and media companies build independent businesses around their work. Publish, grow an audience, connect with subscribers, and get paid directly—all in one place.

Substack combines publishing tools with a network that helps people discover your work through recommendations, Notes, collaborations, and the Substack app. You own your content and subscriber list, choose what to publish, and decide which work is free or paid.

Substack is free to start, with no monthly platform subscription fee. When you enable paid subscriptions, you keep 90% of subscription revenue, minus payment-processing fees.

## When to use Substack

- Start a publication and deliver writing to subscribers by email, on the web, and in the Substack app. [Get started](https://substack.com/get-started.md)
- Host a podcast, distribute episodes to listening apps, and build a community with a companion newsletter and paid subscriptions. [Podcasting](https://substack.com/podcasts.md)
- Publish videos, offer paid exclusives, and connect with subscribers through live video. [Video](https://substack.com/video.md)
- Grow an audience through recommendations, Notes, referrals, collaborations, and discovery in the Substack network. [Growth tools](https://substack.com/growthfeatures.md)
- Build direct relationships with subscribers through comments, Chat, and community discussions. [Features](https://substack.com/features.md)
- Earn directly from your audience with paid subscriptions, choosing which work to make free and which to reserve for paying subscribers. [Going paid](https://substack.com/going-paid.md)
- Run a media business with multiple contributors, newsletters, podcasts, and subscriber communities. [Media founders](https://substack.com/startups.md)
- Bring an existing publication, subscriber list, or podcast to Substack. [Switch to Substack](https://substack.com/switch.md)
- Read, watch, and listen to creators, discover new voices, and participate in their communities. [Substack app](https://substack.com/app.md)

## How agents should use this site

- Use the grouped directory below to find the relevant product, use-case, guide, or comparison page.
- Read the linked Markdown page for detailed capabilities, requirements, pricing, and qualifications.
- When explaining subscription economics, distinguish Substack’s platform fee from payment-processing fees. [Paid subscriptions](https://substack.com/going-paid.md)
- When comparing platforms, preserve the conditions and limitations in the comparison rather than relying on a headline alone.
- For setup instructions and troubleshooting, consult the [Substack Help Center](https://support.substack.com/).

## How to read this site as a machine

The marketing pages in the directory below have plain Markdown versions.
Append `.md` to an indexed page’s URL. For example:
`https://substack.com/podcasts` → `https://substack.com/podcasts.md`.

These Markdown versions preserve substantive page content while removing
navigation, forms, decorative elements, and JavaScript. They are generated
from the corresponding marketing pages and updated with changes to those pages.

Use this file to select individual pages to read. For the complete collection
in one document, use [llms-full.txt](https://substack.com/llms-full.txt).

This directory covers Substack’s own marketing pages. It is not an index of
individual creators’ publications, posts, or subscriber-only content.

## Overview

- [About Substack](https://substack.com/about.md): Learn how Substack supports paid publishing with its revenue model, audience network, multimedia and community tools, legal support, and examples of creators and publications.
- [Substack features](https://substack.com/features.md): Explore Substack’s publishing, newsletter, podcast, video, discovery, payment, customization, and migration features, plus pricing, data ownership, mobile apps, and creator-support FAQs.

## Getting started

- [Distribute your podcast on Substack](https://substack.com/distribute-podcasts-to-substack.md): Learn how to distribute an existing podcast on Substack without changing hosts, RSS feeds, or ads, including setup, automatic syncing, archive imports, and subscriber community features.
- [How to start a Substack](https://substack.com/get-started.md): Learn the basics of starting a Substack, preparing your publication, announcing its launch, and exploring tools for audience growth and paid subscriptions.
- [Move from Ghost to Substack](https://substack.com/ghost.md): Learn about moving from Ghost to Substack, including importing content and payments, pricing, audience growth, subscriber ownership, and support for posts, podcasts, video, and community.
- [Paid subscriptions](https://substack.com/going-paid.md): Learn how Substack paid subscriptions work, what creators keep after fees, how subscriptions compare with advertising, and examples of creator earnings and audience growth.
- [Guide to going paid](https://substack.com/going-paid-guide.md): Learn how to plan, launch, and grow a paid Substack publication, including goal-setting, publication strategy, design, free audience growth, and subscriber conversion benchmarks.
- [Switch to Substack](https://substack.com/switch.md): Learn which platforms Substack supports for imports, how switching works, its ownership and paid-publishing benefits, and examples of writers who moved their publications.

## Publishing and growth

- [Substack app](https://substack.com/app.md): Discover the Substack app for iOS and Android, with video, podcasts, writing, discussions, subscription posts, and chats hosted by writers and creators.
- [Grow your audience](https://substack.com/growthfeatures.md): Learn how Substack supports audience growth through recommendations, creator collaborations, referrals, Boost, app discovery, and SEO, with platform statistics and creator testimonials.
- [Podcasting](https://substack.com/podcasts.md): Learn about Substack's podcast hosting, subscription fees, audience ownership, recording and distribution tools, migration options, and comparisons with other podcast platforms.
- [Video creators on Substack](https://substack.com/tiktok.md): Learn how Substack presents its offering for TikTok and video creators, including subscriptions, live video, chat, discovery, and examples of creators on the platform.
- [Video](https://substack.com/video.md): Learn about Substack’s video creator tools, featured shows, podcast distribution, subscription fees, viewing options, and audience growth, with links to setup guides and support.

## Who Substack is for

- [Authors](https://substack.com/book.md): Learn how authors and publishers can use Substack to connect with readers and promote books, with ownership details, author testimonials, setup steps, and book-marketing resources.
- [Comic book creators](https://substack.com/comic-book-creators.md): Learn how comic book creators use Substack to distribute comics, retain content and adaptation rights, and earn subscription revenue, with examples of featured creators.
- [Food writers](https://substack.com/food-writers.md): Learn how Substack supports food writers with publishing tools, reader communities, and paid subscriptions, with examples of food newsletters and links to creator growth stories.
- [Bloggers](https://substack.com/for-bloggers.md): Learn how Substack supports blogging through web and email publishing, paid subscriptions, and content imports, with examples of established bloggers and resources for growing a publication.
- [Finance writers](https://substack.com/investing-and-business.md): Learn how Substack supports finance writers with subscription publishing, audience growth, content ownership, creator examples, and a comparison with Seeking Alpha and blogs.
- [Local news](https://substack.com/local-news.md): Learn how Substack supports local news publishers through free publishing, paid subscriptions, editorial independence, and community features, with examples of local publications and its 10% revenue fee.
- [Media founders](https://substack.com/startups.md): Learn how Substack supports media founders with publishing tools, subscriptions, audience growth, ownership, migration assistance, and examples of established media businesses.

## Podcasting guides

- [How to Start a Podcast: A Step-by-Step Guide](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast.md): Learn the nine steps to launch a podcast, from choosing a topic and equipment to recording, hosting, distribution, audience growth, and monetization, with Substack features, costs, and FAQs.
- [How to get your podcast on Apple Podcasts](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/apple-podcasts.md): Learn how to submit a Substack podcast to Apple Podcasts, meet feed and artwork requirements, manage updates, troubleshoot delays, and give paid subscribers access through private RSS feeds.
- [How much does it cost to start a podcast?](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/cost.md): Compare free, basic, and full-studio podcast budgets, equipment and hosting prices, music licensing, guest and video costs, and Substack’s paid-subscription fees.
- [Podcast cover art: examples, sizes, and templates](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/cover-art.md): Learn podcast cover art sizes, formats, design principles, free template options, image-rights checks, and how to upload and verify show and episode artwork on Substack.
- [How to edit a podcast with free software](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/editing.md): Learn to edit a podcast for free with Audacity or GarageBand, including cutting mistakes, reducing noise, balancing voices, exporting audio, and publishing with transcripts on Substack.
- [Podcast equipment for beginners: what you need](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/equipment.md): Learn what equipment beginners need for a podcast, including free phone setups, USB versus XLR microphones, solo and two-person budgets, accessories, and recording on Substack.
- [How to start a podcast for free](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/for-free.md): Learn how to launch a podcast for free using existing equipment, compare recording and editing tools, publish on Substack and podcast apps, and understand free-plan limits and optional costs.
- [How to grow a podcast audience](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/grow-audience.md): Learn how to grow a podcast through subscriptions, clips, creator collaborations, Recommendations, search, and community, and track results with Substack’s analytics.
- [How to make money podcasting](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/make-money.md): Learn how podcasts earn through subscriptions, sponsorships, ads, and products, with Substack setup steps, fees, income examples, listening options, and monetization FAQs.
- [How to move your podcast to Substack](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/move-your-podcast.md): Learn how to move a podcast to Substack, redirect RSS feeds, preserve listeners, transfer email and paid subscribers, and keep an existing host if preferred.
- [How to start a paid podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/paid-podcast.md): Learn how to start a paid podcast on Substack, choose subscription benefits, set prices, publish previews, deliver episodes to listening apps, and convert free listeners into paying subscribers.
- [Podcast ideas and topics for your first show](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/podcast-ideas.md): Explore podcast ideas across 11 interests, examples of existing shows, ways to validate a niche, and advice for planning your first five episodes and building a sustainable premise.
- [Podcast name ideas: how to name your show](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/podcast-names.md): Learn how to brainstorm podcast names, compare naming styles, check availability and trademarks, test readability and recall, and finalize or change your show’s name.
- [Podcast script templates and examples](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/podcast-script.md): Learn how to script solo, interview, and co-host podcasts with reusable templates, intro and outro examples, episode structure, timing guidance, and tips for turning scripts into recording outlines.
- [How to record a podcast: a beginner's guide](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/recording.md): Learn how to record a first podcast, choose a setup, prepare your room and microphone, test audio, and record solo or remote interviews with Substack’s free Recording Studio.
- [What is a podcast RSS feed? How to create and use one](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/rss-feed.md): Learn what podcast RSS feeds contain, how to create and distribute one on Substack, how private feeds work, and how to troubleshoot updates or move an existing show.
- [How to get your podcast on Spotify](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/spotify.md): Learn how to connect a Substack podcast to Spotify, manage existing listings, offer paid episodes, upload video, and track listeners, including fees and distribution limitations.
- [How to start a video podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/video-podcast.md): Learn how to plan, equip, record, edit, and distribute a video podcast with Substack, including guest limits, equipment costs, YouTube and Spotify publishing, and monetization options.

## Comparisons

- [Best free podcast hosting](https://substack.com/best-free-podcast-hosting.md): Compare eight free podcast hosts by publishing limits, video, distribution, analytics, audience tools, and revenue fees, with guidance on choosing a host, launching a show, and switching platforms.
- [Best podcast hosting](https://substack.com/best-podcast-hosting.md): Compare 16 podcast hosting platforms by pricing, free-plan limits, video distribution, analytics, monetization, audience ownership, and community features, with Substack's recommendations and FAQs.
- [Substack vs. Acast](https://substack.com/substack-vs-acast.md): Compare Substack and Acast for podcast hosting, subscription fees, ads, audience ownership, video, community tools, and migration, including plan limits and FAQs.
- [Substack vs. beehiiv](https://substack.com/substack-vs-beehiiv.md): Substack’s comparison with beehiiv covers pricing, newsletter tools, podcast hosting limits, audience growth, community features, subscriber ownership, migration, and advertising options.
- [Substack vs. Buzzsprout](https://substack.com/substack-vs-buzzsprout.md): Compare Substack and Buzzsprout for podcast hosting, pricing, subscription fees, audience ownership, community tools, video distribution, and the steps to move a show to Substack.
- [Substack vs. Captivate.fm](https://substack.com/substack-vs-captivate.md): Compare Substack and Captivate.fm podcast hosting costs, membership fees, video distribution, audience ownership, community tools, and steps for moving a show to Substack.
- [Substack vs. Libsyn](https://substack.com/substack-vs-libsyn.md): Compare Substack and Libsyn for podcast hosting, pricing, subscriptions, audience ownership, video, community tools, and distribution, with migration steps and answers to common questions.
- [Substack vs. Patreon](https://substack.com/substack-vs-patreon.md): Substack’s comparison with Patreon covers podcast hosting, publishing, audience growth, community tools, pricing, subscriber ownership, migration limitations, and common creator questions.
- [Substack vs. Podbean](https://substack.com/substack-vs-podbean.md): Compare Substack and Podbean’s podcast hosting, subscription fees, audience ownership, community tools, video features, and free-plan limits, plus steps for moving a show to Substack.
- [Substack vs. Riverside](https://substack.com/substack-vs-riverside.md): Compare Substack and Riverside for podcast hosting, pricing, listener payments, recording, analytics, distribution, and community, with feature tables, migration steps, and FAQs.
- [Substack vs. RSS.com](https://substack.com/substack-vs-rss-com.md): Compare Substack and RSS.com for podcast hosting, pricing, subscriptions, video, audience ownership, and community tools, with feature tables, FAQs, and migration steps.
- [Substack vs. Spotify for Creators](https://substack.com/substack-vs-spotify.md): Compare Substack and Spotify for Creators on podcast hosting, fees, audience ownership, video distribution, community tools, and migration, including limits on transferring paid members.
- [Substack vs. Spreaker](https://substack.com/substack-vs-spreaker.md): Compare Substack and Spreaker for podcast hosting, including fees, supporter payments, advertising, video, community tools, audience ownership, and steps for moving a show.
- [Substack vs. Supercast](https://substack.com/substack-vs-supercast.md): Compare Substack and Supercast for podcast hosting, subscription fees, discovery, community, distribution, and audience ownership, with migration steps and FAQs.
- [Substack vs. Supporting Cast](https://substack.com/substack-vs-supporting-cast.md): Compare Substack and Supporting Cast for podcast pricing, hosting, discovery, audience ownership, and distribution, with feature tables, migration steps, and FAQs.
- [Substack vs. Transistor.fm](https://substack.com/substack-vs-transistor.md): Compare Substack and Transistor.fm for podcast hosting, pricing, paid subscriptions, community tools, distribution, analytics, and the steps for moving a show to Substack.
- [Substack vs. YouTube](https://substack.com/substack-vs-youtube.md): Compare Substack and YouTube for podcasting, including subscription fees, audience ownership, hosting, distribution, community tools, and how to use both platforms together.

## Resources

- [Brand assets](https://substack.com/brand.md): Find Substack logo and wordmark downloads, brand usage rules, media attribution requirements, press contact information, and legal restrictions on using its trademarks.
- [Community and programs](https://substack.com/community-and-programs.md): Learn about Substack’s writer community, peer programs, publishing resources, technical and billing assistance, and legal support through Substack Defender.
- [Substack Defender](https://substack.com/defender.md): Learn how Substack Defender supports publishers facing legal threats, including eligibility, covered countries, case approval, legal-fee limits, and publisher experiences.
- [Resource center](https://substack.com/resources.md): Find Substack guides and creator advice on publishing, growing an audience, paid subscriptions, podcasting, fostering community, and managing a media business.
- [Brand partnerships](https://substack.com/sponsorships.md): Learn about Substack’s brand partnership initiative, audience reach, sponsorship formats, and partner perspectives on supporting creators alongside subscription revenue.

# Substack

> Information from Substack’s public marketing pages.

## About Substack

Source: https://substack.com/about

### Make money doing the work you believe in

Substack presents an alternative to old media models, putting writers, creators, and subscribers in charge.

- **Free to start:** No platform fees, tiers, or contracts to get started. Substack is free to start and free to leave.
- **Earn money right away:** Creators keep 90% of revenue, minus credit card fees. The remainder supports the platform.
- **Build your audience:** Access a platform with 5 million paid subscriptions and counting.
- **Grow faster:** More than half of new subscribers come from Substack’s built-in network.

### Estimate what you could earn on Substack

Substack says a few hundred paid subscribers at $5 per month can replace a salary, while a few thousand can make it a real business. Its business model depends on creators’ success: it only makes money when they do.

The page displays an illustrative earnings figure of **$4,638 per month**, without specifying the inputs in the supplied text. Writers keep **90% of their revenue minus credit card fees**.

### A network that grows with you

Subscribers discover new voices through recommendations, Notes, and collaborations, so creators are not starting from zero.

- **Tens of millions** of people read, watch, and listen on Substack every week.
- **1 million+ posts** are discovered by potential subscribers in the app every day.
- **30%+ of paid subscriptions** come from within Substack’s network.

A testimonial from [Hung Up](https://hunterharris.substack.com/) describes the direct relationship with readers:

> As long as I’ve been on the internet, I feel like I’ve never had this kind of one-to-one relationship with someone who is reading my work.

### Built for every kind of creator

Substack supports solo businesses and full newsrooms, with an emphasis on building a paid subscriber base while owning every word and every direct audience relationship.

#### Media companies

Run a newsroom with multiple writers, sections, and podcasts. Substack handles payments, distribution, and subscriber management.

[Learn more about Substack for media founders](https://substack.com/startups).

#### Writers and journalists

Publish reporting, essays, reviews, and fiction using built-in word-processing and writer-friendly tools. Substack emphasizes writing and publishing without fear.

#### Podcasters and video creators

Host a podcast natively using the Substack Recording Studio, or go live to connect with subscribers immediately. Publish automatically to audiences on Substack, Apple, Spotify, and YouTube, and offer premium episodes to paid subscribers.

#### Experts, educators, and creative voices

Teach, share research, or publish creative work on your own terms. Audiences pay creators directly because they value the work.

#### Legal support for your work

[Substack Defender](https://substack.com/defender/) provides publishers access to legal support, including legal fees, advice, and pre-publication review. Since launching in **2020**, Defender has supported dozens of creators facing alleged defamation, trademark and copyright infringement claims, and other legal issues.

### Who’s here

The page showcases Pulitzer winners, first-time writers, media companies, and solo creators, including:

- **[The Bulwark](https://thebulwark.substack.com/), by The Bulwark team:** Independent news, commentary, and podcasts.
- **[What To Cook When You Don’t Feel Like Cooking](https://whattocook.substack.com/), by Caroline Chambers:** Family-friendly, flavor-packed meals from a recipe developer and food writer.
- **[Lenny’s Newsletter](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/), by Lenny Rachitsky:** Deep dives on product, growth, and careers for builders and operators in tech and beyond.
- **[Fresh Hell](https://tinabrown.substack.com/), by Tina Brown:** Commentary on culture, power, and politics from an editor and media figure.
- **[Magasin](https://magasin.substack.com/), by Laura Reilly:** Fashion, retail, and internet culture through an industry lens.
- **[Zeteo](https://www.zeteo.com/), by Mehdi Hasan:** Interviews and commentary on politics, media, and power, combining video and writing in one subscription.
- **[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar](https://kareem.substack.com/):** Writing on sports, politics, history, and American culture from the NBA legend and award-winning author.
- **[Drop Site News](https://www.dropsitenews.com/):** Investigative reporting and analysis on power, security, and accountability.
- **[Ottolenghi](https://ottolenghi.substack.com/), by Yotam Ottolenghi:** Weekly exclusive recipes, stories, and test kitchen insights from the chef and author.
- **[Caleb Hearon](https://calebsaysthings.substack.com/):** Personal comedy and writing from a stand-up and television performer.
- **[Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/), by Nate Silver:** Data-driven analysis of politics, polling, and media from the founder of FiveThirtyEight.
- **[Story Club](https://georgesaunders.substack.com/), by George Saunders:** Exclusive stories, writing advice, and explorations of craft and character from the Booker Prize-winning author.
- **[The Free Press](https://www.thefp.com/w/the-free-press), by Bari Weiss:** Independent news, essays, and podcasts on stories the page describes as ones mainstream outlets will not touch.
- **[Citrini Research](https://www.citriniresearch.com/):** Macro and markets research, including charts, data, and trade ideas.
- **[Barefoot Contessa](https://inagarten.substack.com/), by Ina Garten:** Recipes and kitchen wisdom, emphasizing approachable, elegant food for home cooks who enjoy hosting.
- **[The Parnas Perspective](https://aaronparnas.substack.com/), by Aaron Parnas:** U.S. and global news explained by an attorney and political commentator.
- **[Making Sense](https://samharris.substack.com/), by Sam Harris:** Philosophy, science, and culture through longform conversations and essays.

A testimonial from [The Honest Broker](https://www.honest-broker.com/) says:

> I’ve never been involved in any media project like Substack. In journalism, you struggle just to stay afloat. Something is changing in media, and I’m fortunate to be part of it.

### Built-in tools

Substack offers tools for publishing, payments, growth, and more, with no technical experience required. It says creators can launch in minutes and build a sustainable business on their own terms.

#### Editor and writing tools

A distraction-free editor supports longform writing, from quick posts to **10,000-word essays**. Creators can format posts, embed media, schedule publications, and manage archives within a single content management system.

#### Multimedia

Written posts, podcasts, live video, and subscriber chat are available in one place, without needing to combine third-party tools or platforms.

#### Built-in growth

Publication recommendations, app-driven discovery, Notes, trending topics, and leaderboards help put creators’ work in front of millions of people for free.

#### Community

Subscriber chats, comment threads, and moderation tools let subscribers participate in a publication rather than only consume its content.

#### Revenue tools

Welcome sequences, win-back campaigns, boosts, and analytics are designed to convert free subscribers into paying subscribers and encourage retention.

A testimonial from [Now What](https://melindawmoyer.substack.com/) describes an additional benefit:

> My book was first published in July 2021, and it continues to sell steadily every week. My editor credits my Substack for helping to drive continued sales.

## Substack app

Source: https://substack.com/app

### The app for independent voices

Discover video, podcasts, and writing, and engage with vibrant communities in the Substack app. Available on [iOS](https://substack.com/app/get-ios) and [Android](https://substack.com/app/get-android).

### World-class video, podcasts, and writing

Stories, ideas, and culture right at your fingertips.

### Exciting discussions

Join interesting and insightful discussions.

### All your subscriptions

Easily find the latest posts from your favorite writers and creators.

### Subscriber chats

Join chats hosted by the writers and creators you love.

## Best free podcast hosting

Source: https://substack.com/best-free-podcast-hosting

### Overview

Compare free podcast hosts by publishing limits, distribution, monetization, and audience tools.

By [Zach Taylor](https://substack.com/@zach1taylor). Last checked: October 21, 2026.

The best free podcast hosting gives a show a permanent home rather than a trial. Free plans differ in episode caps, archive windows, inserted ads, and when fees apply. Audience growth does not automatically require paying for hosting.

**Substack's recommendation:** [Substack](https://substack.com/podcasts) for building an audience and community. Hosting, a website, an email newsletter, and community tools are free; Substack takes a revenue share only when paid subscriptions are enabled.

Other leading choices highlighted on the page are Spotify for Creators for Spotify-centered audiences, RedCircle for unlimited storage and an ad marketplace, RSS.com for simple audio-only hosting, and Spreaker for ad income without a hosting bill.

### Free podcast hosting platforms compared

| Platform | Best for | Free features | Publishing and archive limits | Distribution | When fees apply |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Substack | Building an audience and community | Hosting, video, website, newsletter, community tools, IAB-certified analytics | No episode cap; episodes stay in the feed | Apple Podcasts, including video; Spotify and other apps by RSS; video can publish to YouTube | 10% of paid-subscription revenue, plus credit card fees |
| Spotify for Creators | Audiences mostly on Spotify | Hosting, video, collaboration tools, podcast distribution | No paid plans; video plays only in Spotify, with audio elsewhere | Spotify, plus RSS to Apple Podcasts and other apps | 10% of Memberships, where available |
| RedCircle | Unlimited storage and an ad marketplace | Unlimited storage, episodes, bandwidth, and downloads; analytics; podcast webpage | One podcast; free webpage displays other podcasts under “Related Shows” | Major apps by RSS; free importing and feed redirects | 30% of host-read ads, 50% of programmatic ads, and 12% of exclusive content, plus payment processing |
| RSS.com | Simple audio-only shows | Unlimited episodes for one podcast, IAB-certified analytics, website, distribution | Credit card required before the second episode; 30 days of analytics | Major apps by RSS | Subscriptions require a paid plan and run through Apple, which keeps 30% in the first year |
| Spreaker | Audio ad income without a hosting bill | One podcast, IAB-certified analytics, distribution, Supporters Club | Six months of statistics; Spreaker inserts its own ads | Major apps by RSS; no video | 40% of inserted-ad revenue; 20% of Supporters Club revenue plus payment fees of 5% + $0.25 |
| Acast | Ad-supported shows qualifying for its marketplace | Hosting, IAB-certified analytics, distribution, website on shows.acast.com | Five episodes; further free publishing requires qualifying for and accepting marketplace ads | Major apps by RSS | Paid plans from $25/month; paywalls only through Acast or designated partners |
| Podbean | Listeners using the Podbean app | Hosting, IAB-certified analytics, website, distribution, Podbean app listing | Five total upload hours; latest 20 episodes in feed; Podbean runs ads without paying the creator | Major apps by RSS and Podbean app | Subscriptions through Apple, which keeps 30% in year one, or through Podbean |
| Pinecast | Trying hosting without a credit card | Up to two podcasts, unlimited uploads, basic analytics, distribution | 48MB per episode; latest 10 episodes in feed; older episodes return after upgrading | Standard RSS feed for podcast apps | Monetization tools, including the tip jar, require a paid plan |

**Comparison method:** The page says it checked platforms' own pricing pages, help documentation, and terms, marking a feature as supported only when documented.

### What free podcast hosting includes

A podcast host stores audio and video files and generates a show's RSS feed. Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other listening apps read that feed to list shows and deliver episodes; in this role they are directories rather than hosts. Most require a one-time feed submission, after which new episodes appear automatically.

YouTube distributes video but is not a complete podcast-hosting solution: it does not send an RSS feed to podcast apps.

“Free” can mean several things:

- **Ongoing free plans:** Continued publishing without paying, such as Substack, Spotify for Creators, and RedCircle Core.
- **Limited free plans:** Caps on episodes, upload hours, file size, archives, or analytics, such as Acast, Podbean, RSS.com, and Pinecast.
- **Conditional free plans:** Hosting in exchange for ads inserted into the show, such as Spreaker and Podbean's free plan.
- **Time-limited plans and trials:** Buzzsprout removes free-plan episodes after 90 days; RedCircle's paid plans begin with a seven-day trial.
- **Paid bundles:** Hosting included with another paid product, such as Riverside recording plans.

#### Free trials and paid bundles excluded from the comparison

- [Buzzsprout](https://substack.com/substack-vs-buzzsprout): Free-plan episodes are removed after 90 days. Paid plans start at $15/month, billed annually.
- [Riverside](https://substack.com/substack-vs-riverside): Hosting is available only with paid plans, starting at $29/month.
- [Captivate.fm](https://substack.com/substack-vs-captivate): No free plan; paid plans start at $19/month.
- [Transistor.fm](https://substack.com/substack-vs-transistor): No free plan; paid plans start at $19/month.
- [Libsyn](https://substack.com/substack-vs-libsyn): No free plan; paid plans start at $8/month.

### How to choose a free podcast host

- **Publishing frequency:** Five total upload hours on Podbean or five episodes on Acast can be exhausted quickly. Weekly shows need a host without an episode cap.
- **Archive retention:** Podbean exposes the latest 20 episodes, Pinecast the latest 10, and Buzzsprout removes free-plan episodes after 90 days.
- **Distribution:** Look for an RSS feed accepted by Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other apps. Most directories require one-time submission; Spotify for Creators publishes directly to Spotify.
- **Video:** Substack provides free video to Apple Podcasts and can publish to YouTube. Spotify's free video plays only in Spotify. RSS.com, Acast, Podbean, and RedCircle charge for video; Spreaker does not support it. [Compare video podcast hosting platforms](https://substack.com/best-podcast-hosting#video-podcast-hosting).
- **Audience tools:** A feed distributes a show but does not identify listeners. Consider an email list you own, a website, audience conversation tools, and a discovery network. The page says only Substack includes all four among these free hosts.
- **Monetization:** Compare both the percentage and what it applies to: 10% of Substack paid subscriptions, 10% of Spotify Memberships, 12% of RedCircle exclusive content, or 20% of Spreaker Supporters Club revenue, before applicable processing fees. Advertising platforms also split revenue. Weigh fees against new paying subscribers the platform brings.
- **Migration:** Check import and RSS redirect support so existing listeners remain subscribed. Paid subscribers transfer readily only when you own the payment relationship. When Apple, Spotify, or Podbean processes payments, moving requires each paying subscriber to re-enter a card, and some will not. Pinecast's free plan lacks an import tool.

The page ranks hosts using six criteria:

1. An ongoing free plan rather than a trial.
2. No episode cap or episode removal.
3. No host-inserted ads.
4. No credit card requirement.
5. Distribution to Apple Podcasts and Spotify.
6. IAB-certified download analytics.

It states that Substack meets all six.

### How to host a podcast for free

1. **Choose an ongoing free host** to avoid having to move later.
2. **Create the show:** Add its name, artwork, description, and category.
3. **Publish the first episode:** Directories require at least one episode before accepting a feed.
4. **Check the RSS feed:** Confirm its title, artwork, and category, which apps read from the feed.
5. **Submit to directories:** Use Apple Podcasts Connect for a one-time submission. On Substack, connect Spotify in podcast settings.

### When a paid podcast host may be worthwhile

Audience growth alone does not require paid hosting. Substack hosting remains free as a show grows, with fees applying only to paid-subscription earnings.

A paid host may be worthwhile for specific needs:

- Several shows under one account, as with Transistor plans.
- Private team or company feeds, as with Captivate's private podcasting.
- An advertising marketplace that sells ads for you, such as Acast's.
- Recording, editing, and hosting in one tool, such as Riverside.

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is the best free podcast hosting platform?

The page recommends Substack for audience and community building because hosting, video, a website, a newsletter, and community tools are free and its growth network supports discovery. Spotify for Creators is presented as the simplest alternative for audiences almost entirely on Spotify.

#### Is Substack free for podcast hosting?

Yes. Free shows receive the same tools as paid shows. If paid subscriptions are enabled, payments use the creator's Stripe account, and the creator keeps 90% less credit card fees.

#### Can I host a podcast for free permanently?

Yes. Substack, Spotify for Creators, and RedCircle Core offer ongoing free plans without episode caps. Other plans have limits: Acast allows five episodes before marketplace conditions apply, Podbean allows five total upload hours, Pinecast shows the latest 10 episodes, and Buzzsprout removes free-plan episodes after 90 days.

#### Can I distribute a free podcast to Spotify and Apple Podcasts?

Yes. Free hosts provide RSS feeds for listening apps. Apple Podcasts requires one-time submission through Apple Podcasts Connect. Substack connects to Spotify through podcast settings; Spotify for Creators publishes there directly.

#### Which free podcast hosts support video?

Substack hosts video free, delivers it to Apple Podcasts, and can publish it to YouTube. Spotify for Creators offers free video only within Spotify. YouTube distributes video but does not provide an RSS feed to podcast apps. RSS.com, Acast, Podbean, and RedCircle require paid video plans; Spreaker does not support video.

#### Can I make money with free podcast hosting?

Yes. Before payment processing, Substack takes 10% of paid subscriptions, Spotify 10% of Memberships, RedCircle 12% of exclusive content, and Spreaker's free plan 20% of Supporters Club revenue. RedCircle keeps 30% of host-read ad revenue and 50% of programmatic ad revenue; Spreaker keeps 40% of inserted-ad revenue. Consider whether a platform also brings new paying subscribers.

#### Can I switch hosts without losing subscribers?

Usually. An RSS redirect from the old host lets podcast apps follow the show to its new host. Confirm redirect support before moving. Paid subscriber migration depends on ownership of the payment relationship; Apple-, Spotify-, or Podbean-managed payments require subscribers to re-enter payment details.

#### What happens when I reach a free-plan limit?

It depends on the host. Acast stops at five episodes unless the show qualifies for and accepts marketplace ads; Podbean caps total uploads at five hours. Pinecast and Podbean expose only the latest 10 and 20 episodes respectively, while Buzzsprout removes free-plan episodes after 90 days. Upgrading lifts limits, and Pinecast restores older episodes to the feed.

### What is podcast hosting?

Podcast hosting stores audio and video files and generates a show's RSS feed. Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other podcast apps read that feed to list shows and deliver new episodes.

Spotify serves both roles: its listening app plays podcasts, while Spotify for Creators provides hosting. YouTube hosts video but does not send an RSS feed to Apple Podcasts or Spotify, so it is not a complete cross-platform podcast hosting solution.

Some hosts provide only storage and a feed. Others also provide a website, newsletter, payments, and community tools.

- **Distribution:** Look for Apple Podcasts and Spotify distribution. For video, check Apple Podcasts and YouTube support rather than support limited to a single app.
- **Analytics:** IAB Tech Lab certification matters for sponsor-trusted download figures. Following IAB guidelines is not the same as certification.
- **Monetization:** Compare subscription fees, inserted ads, ad marketplaces, and earning eligibility thresholds.
- **Portability:** Check feed redirects, episode exports, and subscriber portability. Moving paying subscribers depends on owning the payment relationship. The page warns that when Apple, Spotify, Patreon, or Buzzsprout handles payments, subscribers must re-enter their cards when moving, and some will not.

For beginners, the page recommends free hosting without an episode cap that can accommodate growth: Substack, or Spotify for Creators for a Spotify-focused audience.

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is the best podcast hosting platform for beginners?

The page recommends Substack for free hosting without an episode cap, distribution to Apple Podcasts and Spotify, and built-in newsletter, community, and paid subscriptions. Spotify for Creators is its simplest free alternative for Spotify-only priorities. See [how to start a podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast) for a walkthrough.

#### Can you host a podcast for free?

Yes. Substack, Spotify for Creators, and YouTube provide ongoing free hosting, though YouTube does not distribute an RSS feed to other podcast apps.

Other free plans have restrictions: Buzzsprout removes episodes after 90 days; Acast caps hosting at 5 episodes; Podbean allows 5 total upload hours and inserts its own ads; RSS.com requires a credit card before episode two; Spreaker inserts ads; and beehiiv allows 5,000 downloads/month.

#### How much does podcast hosting cost?

Among the platforms in this guide, published costs range from free to $250/month. Substack, Spotify for Creators, YouTube, and Patreon charge nothing to host. Paid plans range from Libsyn's $8/month to Spreaker's $250/month, with most starting between $12 and $29/month.

Many also take subscription revenue shares, ranging from 0% on beehiiv paid plans to 30% for YouTube memberships and Apple Podcasts Subscriptions. The individual reviews note Apple's reduction to 15% after the first year.

#### Do you need podcast hosting to publish on Spotify and Apple Podcasts?

Yes. These apps read the RSS feed generated by a podcast host. Spotify for Creators is also a host, but its video plays only within Spotify. YouTube hosts video without providing an RSS feed to Apple Podcasts or Spotify.

#### Can you switch podcast hosting platforms without losing subscribers?

Usually. A redirect from the old RSS feed to the new one lets podcast apps follow the show while keeping listeners subscribed. Creators can also update feed URLs in Apple Podcasts Connect and Spotify for Creators. Confirm that the old host supports redirects before moving.

Paid subscriptions are harder to move. Creators can bring them along only when they own the payment relationship. If Apple, Spotify, Patreon, or the host manages payments, subscribers usually need to sign up again.

### Defender has your back

Substack created Defender to help independent journalists and creators respond to spurious legal threats from wealthy and powerful interests seeking to silence reporting and opinions. Qualifying participants can receive support in defending against these abuses, helping create a climate where publishers can speak freely.

## Distribute your podcast on Substack

Source: https://substack.com/distribute-podcasts-to-substack

### Your podcast stays where it is. Now it's on Substack, too.

Keep your hosting platform, RSS feed, and ads. Add Substack as another place your show lives.

### A listening surface you're not on yet

Substack is already a podcast listening and community app. Millions of people open the Substack app every day to discover, listen, and subscribe. Distributing your podcast to Substack puts your episodes where those listeners already spend time—without changing your hosting platform, ads, or feed.

### Nothing about your podcast business changes

Continue hosting your podcast where it is today, with the same RSS feed and dynamically inserted ads. Substack becomes one more place where listeners can find and follow your show. Setup takes three steps:

1. **Paste your podcast RSS feed.** Substack scans your show details, artwork, and episode catalog.
2. **Review your show on Substack.** Your title, description, artwork, and settings are prefilled from your feed. You can edit anything before going live.
3. **Go live.** Choose whether to auto-publish new episodes and whether to import your back catalog. New episodes sync automatically.

### Turn listeners into subscribers, and subscribers into a community

Build an audience that comes back between episodes with newsletters, chat, and paid subscriptions.

#### Discovery from the Substack network

Substack's discovery feed and recommendations feature power growth across the platform, putting your work in front of millions.

#### Own your audience

On Substack, you own your relationship with subscribers, including their email address and payment relationship if you enable paid subscriptions.

#### One home for the world around your show

The page presents Substack as a place where your podcast can live alongside a subscriber community, writing, and paid subscriptions, helping it grow beyond the episode.

### Already on Substack?

If you're already publishing on Substack, you can connect your podcast's RSS feed. Your existing subscribers can discover, follow, and listen to your show without leaving Substack.

### Questions about how syncing works

#### Does Substack create a new RSS feed or store my audio?

No. Substack reads from your existing RSS feed. Your audio, ads, and analytics stay intact in your hosting platform. Substack works as another listening surface, not a separate audio path.

#### Do I have to move my podcast to a new hosting platform?

No. Your hosting platform doesn't change. Substack reads from it.

#### Can I keep dynamic ads?

Yes. Synced episodes keep using your external audio URL, so ads configured in your hosting platform continue to run on Substack.

#### Will new episodes publish automatically?

Yes, if you turn on auto-publish. You can also leave auto-publish off and review each episode as a draft before it goes live.

#### Can I import my back catalog?

Yes. During setup, you can choose to import your existing episode archive to Substack.

#### Will archive imports notify subscribers?

No. Imported episodes don't send subscriber notifications. Only new episodes you publish going forward send notifications.

#### Can I review new episodes before they go live?

Yes. Turn off auto-publish, and synced episodes will save as drafts for you to review first.

#### Can I host my podcast on Substack?

Yes. Substack also offers podcast hosting and automatic distribution to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and any other podcast app that accepts an RSS feed. See [How do I create and publish a podcast on Substack?](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037462092-How-do-I-create-and-publish-a-podcast-on-Substack).

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is Substack?

Substack is a publishing platform where writers, podcasters, and video creators build subscription-based publications. It combines newsletter delivery, podcast hosting, native video, community, and a built-in discovery network. Creators own their content and subscriber lists.

#### How much does Substack cost?

Substack is free to use, with no upfront costs, monthly fees, or subscriber limits on the free tier. It takes a **10% revenue share** when creators earn through paid subscriptions. The podcast FAQ clarifies that creators keep **90% before standard Stripe processing fees**.

#### Can I use my own domain on Substack?

Yes. Connect an existing domain or buy one through the platform. Substack supports DNS configuration and apex-domain redirects.

#### Can I import my subscribers from another platform?

Yes. Upload a CSV with list cleaning and validation, or import paid subscribers directly from Stripe. Content imports are supported from WordPress, Ghost, Medium, Beehiiv, Mailchimp, Tumblr, Webflow, and other platforms.

#### Can I export my data from Substack?

Yes. Export full publication data at any time, including posts as CSV and HTML, the complete subscriber list, and optional statistics. Creators retain ownership of their content and audience.

#### Does Substack support podcasting?

Yes. [Podcast hosting](https://substack.com/podcasts) has no monthly hosting fee. Features include free and paid episodes, private feeds, automatic RSS distribution to Apple Podcasts and Spotify, email delivery, YouTube publishing for video podcasts, recording tools, download analytics, and transcripts.

Spotify Open Access combines free and paid episodes in one synced feed, with a flow for connecting subscriptions or upgrading. Text-to-speech narration is available to some creators. See the guide to [starting a podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast).

#### Does Substack support video?

Yes. [Native video hosting](https://substack.com/video), live video with real-time chat, automatic YouTube and LinkedIn distribution, clipping, captions, and RTMP connections to external streaming software are supported.

#### How does Substack help me grow my audience?

Through cross-publication recommendations, category leaderboards, Explore, Notes, restacks, reader referrals, and semantic search. The page claims that no other newsletter platform offers an equivalent built-in discovery network.

#### What makes Substack different from Mailchimp, Beehiiv, or Ghost?

The page positions Substack as the only newsletter platform with a built-in social and discovery network. It contrasts its combination of publishing, recommendations, Notes, leaderboards, and Explore with competitors’ focus on email delivery and marketing automation. It also says most competitors do not offer native podcast hosting and live video streaming.

#### Does Substack have an app?

Yes. Native iOS and Android apps support reading, subscribing, podcasts, video, chat, and subscription management. Creators can view earnings and statistics on mobile.

#### Can I accept payments through Substack?

Yes. Stripe-powered payments support monthly and annual subscriptions, founding-member tiers, trials, coupons, gifts, group billing, and multiple currencies.

#### Can I customize the design of my Substack?

Yes. A visual editor provides multiple homepage layouts, colors and fonts, email CSS, navigation editing, logo and favicon uploads, and modular content blocks, without requiring code.

#### Does Substack provide legal support for writers and creators?

Yes. Substack Defender offers access to legal support as part of Substack’s efforts to uphold a free press and free speech. It provides protection against certain types of claims and access to advice and support for publishers facing legal uncertainty or pressure because of their work.

## How to Start a Podcast: A Step-by-Step Guide

Source: https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast

### Overview

Last updated: October 30, 2026. By [Linda Lebrun](https://substack.com/@linda), Substack.

Starting a podcast involves nine steps: choose a topic and audience, select a format and schedule, name the show and create artwork, get equipment, record and edit, choose a host, distribute to podcast apps, grow an audience, and establish ways to earn money.

Substack offers free hosting for audio and video podcasts, distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other apps, and delivery of episodes to subscribers by email. According to [Podnews](https://podnews.net/update/substack-podcast-tab), creators who publish podcasts on Substack collectively earn over $200 million a year.

### Step 1: Choose a topic and an audience

Choose a topic you can discuss for **50 or more episodes**, with a specific group of people who want to hear about it. A narrow topic is easier to grow than a broad one because listeners can quickly tell whether the show is for them.

Test the topic by writing down **10 episode ideas**:

- If you cannot come up with 10, the topic is too narrow.
- If the ideas could belong to any show, the topic is too broad.

A topic related to what you already write or post about can help turn your blog, newsletter, or social media following into your first listeners. Browse the Apple Podcasts and Spotify charts in your category to identify angles existing shows do not cover well.

Related guide: [Podcast ideas and topics for your first show](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/podcast-ideas).

### Step 2: Choose a format and a schedule

The three most common formats are solo shows, interviews, and co-hosted conversations. Choose one you can sustain every week or every two weeks.

| Format | What it requires | Suits | Example on Substack |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solo | One host | Experts, commentators, writers | [Letters from an American](https://heathercoxrichardson.substack.com/podcast), Heather Cox Richardson’s narrated audio version of her daily newsletter |
| Interview | A steady supply of guests | Hosts with a network in their field | [Dwarkesh Podcast](https://www.dwarkesh.com/), Dwarkesh Patel’s long-form interviews with researchers, historians, and technology leaders |
| Co-hosted | Two or three regular hosts with chemistry | Friends, colleagues, debate formats | [Three Ingredients](https://threeingredients.substack.com/), where Ruth Reichl, Nancy Silverton, and Laurie Ochoa discuss food each week |

Make three additional decisions:

- **Audio only or video:** Video can reach viewers on YouTube and in-app feeds. Short video clips are the main way podcasts are shared on social media. On Substack, one upload can serve as a video episode, an audio episode, and a written post.
- **Episode length:** The typical episode is about **35 minutes**, according to [CastFox Research, 2026](https://www.castfox.net/research/average-podcast-episode-length-2026). Match the length to your content and keep it consistent.
- **Schedule:** Publish on the same day each week or every two weeks. Reliability matters more than frequency.

Related guide: [How to start a video podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/video-podcast).

### Step 3: Name your podcast and create cover art

Choose a name that clearly tells potential listeners what the show covers. Use words your audience would search for: descriptive names are easier to find than abstract ones. If you already have an audience, including your own name can help them find the show.

Podcast apps require square cover art. Apple Podcasts requires artwork between **1400 × 1400 and 3000 × 3000 pixels**. Keep the title large and legible at thumbnail size.

Related guides:

- [Podcast name ideas: how to name your show](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/podcast-names)
- [Podcast cover art: examples, sizes, and templates](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/cover-art)

### Step 4: Get the equipment you need

You can start with just a phone, but a microphone and headphones improve sound quality.

- **USB microphone:** Connects directly to a computer and is the simplest beginner option. If the room is not perfectly quiet, choose a dynamic microphone, designed to pick up your voice and block background sound.
- **Closed-back headphones:** Prevent a guest’s audio from leaking into your microphone.
- **Recording space:** Add a rug or other soft surfaces to reduce noise and echo.
- **Video equipment:** A webcam or phone camera is enough to start. Place the light source in front of you, not behind you.

#### How much does it cost to start a podcast?

You can start for close to **$0** with a phone and free hosting. A typical beginner setup costs approximately **$100–$300**.

| Item | Typical retail price (USD) |
|---|---|
| USB microphone | $50–$150 |
| Closed-back headphones | $30–$100 |
| Webcam for video podcasts | $50–$150 |
| Recording software | $0 with Substack Recording Studio |
| Hosting and distribution | $0 on Substack |

Related guides:

- [How to start a podcast for free](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/for-free)
- [How much does it cost to start a podcast?](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/cost)
- [Podcast equipment for beginners](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/equipment)

### Step 5: Record and edit your first episodes

Record with a microphone and headphones in a quiet room, using software on your computer or phone. Invite remote guests through a browser-based recording tool.

Substack Recording Studio lets you record solo episodes or conversations with **up to two guests** from a desktop browser, without separate recording software. You can share your screen with co-hosts and add a watermark. After recording, Substack creates clips and thumbnails for sharing.

You can also livestream on Substack from desktop or the app, including with an audio-only option, and publish the recording as an episode.

**Recording tips:**

- Record a **30-second test** and listen back before every session.
- Keep the microphone a constant distance from your mouth—approximately one hand-width.
- For remote interviews, ask guests to use headphones, an external microphone, and a reliable internet connection.

**Editing:** Remove long pauses, false starts, and off-topic sections. Adjust volume so every voice is at the same level. Natural conversation is acceptable; there is no need to over-edit.

**Transcripts:** A transcript improves searchability and accessibility for people who prefer to read. Substack automatically creates a transcript for each video podcast, which you can add to the episode’s post.

Related guides:

- [How to record a podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/recording)

- [How to edit a podcast with free software](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/editing)

### Step 6: Choose a podcast host and publish

A podcast host stores your audio files and creates the **RSS feed** that podcast apps use to list your show. You need a host before appearing on Apple Podcasts or Spotify.

Compare hosts on five factors:

1. Cost.
2. Distribution to major apps.
3. Video support.
4. Whether you receive listeners’ contact details.
5. Ways to earn money.

#### Hosting on Substack

- **Free hosting and distribution:** Substack does not charge to host or distribute a podcast. Paid subscriptions can provide bonus content or ad-free episodes. You keep **90% of earnings, minus credit card processing fees**.
- **Audio and video:** Publish audio episodes, video episodes, and livestreams in one place.
- **Email delivery:** New episodes go to subscribers by email and appear in the Substack app and major podcast apps.
- **Subscriber-list ownership:** You receive subscribers’ email addresses and can export the list at any time.
- **Posts alongside episodes:** Add show notes, essays, transcripts, and comments to an episode’s post.
- **Download statistics:** Substack’s podcast download measurement is [certified by IAB Tech Lab](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/20501349089300-Are-Substack-podcast-analytics-IAB-certified), supporting sponsor pitches and performance reporting.

#### Set up a podcast on Substack

1. Go to [substack.com](https://substack.com) and select **Start your Substack**. Create a free account and name your publication using your podcast’s name or your own name.
2. Open **Dashboard** from the top-right corner of your publication’s page.
3. Select the **Podcast** tab, then **Start your podcast**.
4. Enter the title, description, category, and language, and upload cover art.

If you already host a podcast elsewhere, choose **Import an existing podcast** and paste your current RSS feed URL.

Related guides:

- [What is a podcast RSS feed? How to create and use one](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/rss-feed)
- [How to move your podcast to Substack](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/move-your-podcast)
- [Best podcast hosting platforms](https://substack.com/best-podcast-hosting), comparing Substack, Buzzsprout, Spotify, YouTube, and other hosts on the five factors above

### Step 7: Distribute to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other apps

Submit your podcast’s RSS feed URL to each podcast app once. New episodes then appear automatically.

On Substack:

- **Spotify:** In podcast settings, select **Connect to Spotify**. Substack sends both free and paid episodes. Paid episodes display a padlock; paying subscribers unlock them by linking their Substack account in Spotify.
- **Apple Podcasts, Overcast, Pocket Casts, and others:** Copy the RSS feed URL from the Podcast tab settings and submit it to each directory.

**Your RSS URL will not be accepted until you publish an episode.** Create your first episode before submitting the feed.

Substack podcasters upload each episode once for distribution to podcast apps. For example, Shea Serrano and Jason Concepcion launched [Organizing Things](https://goodmovie.substack.com/) on Substack in **September 2026**, reaching their existing newsletter audience and listeners on other podcast apps at the same time.

The first episode was free on Substack, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and YouTube, and received **more than 10,000 downloads in its first week**, with no paid promotion. [Read the launch example](https://on.substack.com/p/shea-serrano-podcast).

Related guides:

- [How to get your podcast on Apple Podcasts](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/apple-podcasts)
- [How to get your podcast on Spotify](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/spotify)

### Step 8: Grow your audience

Guests, clips, and recommendations from other creators are the most direct growth methods for a new podcast.

- **Post short clips:** Share highlights on social media. Substack identifies key moments from recordings and livestreams and turns them into clips. The page reports that clips made on Substack have brought in [nearly 500,000 free subscriptions](https://on.substack.com/p/new-livestreaming-from-desktop) since launch. Clips can be shared to Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, or YouTube Shorts in one tap. Linking YouTube allows Substack to automatically upload the **top two clips from each livestream** to your Shorts channel. See [how to connect YouTube and post Shorts](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/30627373184532-How-can-I-connect-my-YouTube-account-to-my-Substack#h_01JYYT0WNM5EHNEHTPVHXK23E8).
- **Collaborate:** Invite guests with their own audiences and appear on other shows. On Substack, creators can co-host livestreams and recommend each other’s publications. [Creator Match](https://on.substack.com/i/212722695/creator-match) helps find creators with similar audience sizes and interests, with direct messaging from its dashboard.
- **Publish the episode as a post:** A summary or transcript can rank in search; a standalone audio file cannot.
- **Ask listeners to subscribe:** Mention subscribing at the beginning and end of each episode. Subscribers receive new episodes automatically, including by email on Substack.

Related guide: [How to grow a podcast audience](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/grow-audience).

### Step 9: Make money from your podcast

Podcasts can earn money through **paid subscriptions, sponsorships, and related products**. Paid subscriptions provide recurring revenue that does not rely on download numbers.

On Substack:

- Keep free episodes public and put bonus episodes, early access, or full archives behind a paywall.
- Paying subscribers can listen in the Substack app, on Spotify, or in any podcast app through a private RSS feed.
- There are no hosting fees. When paid subscriptions are enabled, you keep **90% of earnings, minus credit card processing fees**.

Many podcasters offer paying subscribers additional benefits. Scott Galloway, for example, publishes bonus episodes and ad-free versions for paid subscribers on Substack. See [how podcasters use subscriptions and sponsorships](https://on.substack.com/p/introducing-podcast-sponsorships).

- [How to start a paid podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/paid-podcast)

### Frequently asked questions

#### How do I start a podcast for free?

Record on a phone or computer using free software, then publish on a free host. Substack provides recording, hosting, and distribution at no cost. Substack Recording Studio supports recording audio directly in a browser.

#### How do I start a podcast with no experience?

Choose one topic, record a **20-minute solo episode** with the equipment you have, and publish it. Most hosts improve with repetition. For best results, record **two or three episodes before launch** so you can review your delivery.

#### What do you need to start a podcast?

A topic, microphone, headphones, quiet recording space, recording software, and a podcast host. You can start with only a phone and a free host such as Substack.

#### Can I start a podcast on my phone?

Yes. A phone can record audio and video. You can livestream from the Substack mobile app and publish the recording as an episode. To record without going live, use Substack Recording Studio on a computer or in the Substack phone app. You can also record with a third-party tool, such as Riverside, and upload the episode to Substack.

#### How long should a podcast episode be?

According to [CastFox Research, 2026](https://www.castfox.net/research/average-podcast-episode-length-2026):

- A typical episode is about **35 minutes**.
- Half of all podcasts have episodes between **18 and 56 minutes**.
- Kids and family shows are shortest, at about **24 minutes**.
- TV and film shows are longest, at about **59 minutes**.

Choose a length that fits the topic and keep it consistent. On Substack, you can publish a short free episode and a longer version for paid subscribers.

#### How do podcasts make money?

Through paid subscriptions, sponsorships, and related products. [Paid subscriptions on Substack](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/paid-podcast) let listeners pay creators directly. According to [Podnews](https://podnews.net/update/substack-podcast-tab), creators publishing podcasts on Substack collectively earn over **$200 million a year**.

#### How do I get my podcast on Spotify and Apple Podcasts?

Publish with a podcast host, then submit your RSS feed to each app. On Substack, select **Connect to Spotify** in podcast settings and submit the RSS feed URL to Apple Podcasts.

#### Do I need a website for my podcast?

A website helps listeners discover the show in search and provides a place for show notes. On Substack, your publication serves as the podcast website, and each episode has its own page.

#### Can I host a podcast on Substack?

Yes. Substack hosts audio and video podcasts for free and distributes them to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other podcast apps. Episodes also go to subscribers by email, and creators can earn money through paid subscriptions.

## How to get your podcast on Apple Podcasts

Source: https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/apple-podcasts

### Getting your podcast on Apple Podcasts

Submit your show's RSS feed to Apple Podcasts once, for free, and every new episode you publish appears there automatically.

Last updated: October 27, 2026 · By [Linda Lebrun](https://substack.com/@linda), Substack

To get your podcast on Apple Podcasts, copy your show's RSS feed URL from your podcast host and submit it in Apple Podcasts Connect. Apple reviews the show before listing it.

On Substack, your RSS feed is created for free when you set up a podcast, with no hosting fees and no platform fees. The process is:

1. Prepare an Apple Account, a published episode, and complete show details.
2. Copy your RSS feed URL from Substack.
3. Submit your show in Apple Podcasts Connect.
4. Add your Apple Podcasts link to Substack.

This guide is part of Substack's [complete guide to starting a podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast).

### What do you need before you submit to Apple Podcasts?

- **An Apple Account.** Sign in to Apple Podcasts Connect with your Apple Account. An existing account needs two-factor authentication turned on. Apple may ask for a payment method, but you aren't charged unless you make a purchase.
- **At least one published episode.** Apple Podcasts lists a show only when it has at least one episode, and Substack's feed is accepted only after you publish one. If your first full episode isn't ready, publish a short trailer introducing the show.
- **Complete show details.** Apple asks for accurate, complete details, including categories. On Substack, your show's title, description, byline, language, categories, and explicit content setting come from the **Basics** section of your podcast settings.
- **Cover art that meets Apple's requirements.** Your cover must be square, between **1400 × 1400 and 3000 × 3000 pixels**, and saved as a **JPEG or PNG in RGB color**. For examples and templates, see [podcast cover art](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/cover-art).

The Basics section controls the details Apple Podcasts shows on your show page. Changes saved there appear in your RSS feed right away. The page illustrates these settings with the sample podcast Skyline Trails.

If your show is already on Apple Podcasts with another host, **you don't need to submit it again**. See [how to move your podcast to Substack](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/move-your-podcast).

### How to copy your RSS feed for Apple Podcasts on Substack

Your RSS feed URL is the web address Apple Podcasts uses to find your show and its episodes. Substack creates it at no cost.

1. Open your publication's **Settings** and scroll to **Podcasts**.
2. Select **Edit** next to your podcast.
3. In the Apple Podcasts section, select **Copy URL**.

For more background, see [what a podcast RSS feed is](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/rss-feed).

### How to submit a podcast to Apple Podcasts

Apple Podcasts Connect is Apple's tool for adding and managing shows on Apple Podcasts.

1. In the Apple Podcasts section of your Substack podcast settings, select **Visit Apple Podcasts Connect**, or go directly to [Apple Podcasts Connect](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/).
2. Sign in with your Apple Account. The first time, accept Apple's terms.
3. Select the **Add (+)** button, then **New Show**.
4. Choose **Add a show with an RSS feed**, paste your RSS feed URL, and select **Add**.
5. Check the show information Apple takes from your feed. Then set your content rights and contact information.
6. Under **Availability**, choose the countries or regions where your show appears.
7. Select **Save**, then publish your show.

Apple checks your feed before you can publish and displays a warning if it finds a problem. Fix the issue, then try again.

After you publish, Apple reviews your show against its content guidelines. **Apple doesn't give a set review time.** It emails you when your show's status changes, and its approval email includes a link to your show on Apple Podcasts.

### How to add your Apple Podcasts link to Substack

When your show is live, add its Apple Podcasts link to Substack so listeners can find it from your episodes:

1. Copy your show's Apple Podcasts link from Apple's approval email or your show's details in Apple Podcasts Connect.
2. Paste it into the Apple Podcasts section of your Substack podcast settings and select **Save**.

Your Substack episodes then list Apple Podcasts under **Listen on**. The page illustrates this with an Open Tab episode, where listeners can choose the Substack app, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or an RSS feed.

### What happens after your podcast is on Apple Podcasts?

Once your show is listed, you don't need to submit anything again. Every episode you publish on Substack goes to your RSS feed, and Apple Podcasts picks it up automatically.

- **New episodes:** Apple checks your feed on its own schedule, so a new episode can take **up to 24 hours** to appear.
- **Missing episodes:** If an episode still isn't there after 24 hours, sign in to Apple Podcasts Connect, select your show, and select **Refresh Feed**.
- **Changes to your show:** A new title, description, or cover goes through your feed. Apple Podcasts can take **up to 24 hours** to show it.
- **Video episodes:** Before publishing a video episode on Substack, turn on **Add audio to podcast RSS feed**. Apple Podcasts listeners then hear its audio. See [how to start a video podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/video-podcast).

Examples of podcasts distributed this way include:

- [Open Tab](https://on.substack.com/s/open-tab), Substack's interview show with independent media founders, has its own [Apple Podcasts page](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/open-tab/id1896276138), which Apple colors to match the show's orange-red cover.
- [Organizing Things](https://goodmovie.substack.com/podcast), from Shea Serrano and Jason Concepcion, publishes each episode on Substack, then [distributes it automatically](https://on.substack.com/p/shea-serrano-podcast) to YouTube, Spotify, and [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/organizing-things-with-jason-and-shea/id6805726486).

Related guides explain [how to get your podcast on Spotify](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/spotify) and [how to grow a podcast audience](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/grow-audience).

### How do paid subscribers listen on Apple Podcasts?

On Substack, paid subscribers hear your paid episodes in Apple Podcasts through a **private RSS feed**. You don't need to set up anything in Apple Podcasts Connect for this.

Each subscriber gets a feed unique to them, and a paid subscriber's feed includes your paid episodes. To add it, a subscriber:

1. Opens your publication's **Manage subscription** page, finds **Private podcast feed**, selects **Set up podcast**, and copies the feed address.
2. In Apple Podcasts, goes to **Library**, taps the three dots, and selects **Add a Show by URL**.

Free listeners on Apple Podcasts hear your free episodes and any free previews of paid episodes. When you turn on paid subscriptions, **you keep 90% of what you earn, minus credit card fees**. See [how to start a paid podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/paid-podcast).

Apple also offers the **Apple Podcasters Program**, which lets you sell subscriptions inside Apple Podcasts for an annual fee of **$19.99 in the US**. You don't need it to list a free show or to reach your Substack paid subscribers on Apple Podcasts.

Substack is also adding [podcast sponsorships](https://on.substack.com/p/introducing-podcast-sponsorships). Dynamic sponsorships, described as being in early access, let you run campaigns with your own sponsors and update ads across your back catalog without re-editing episodes. Participation is optional; you decide how many ads run and which kinds of sponsors you accept. See [how to make money podcasting](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/make-money) for more ways to earn.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Can you upload a podcast directly to Apple Podcasts?

For most shows, no. Apple Podcasts gets episodes from your host's RSS feed, so you submit the feed once and new episodes appear automatically. Apple Podcasts Connect takes direct audio uploads only for subscriber episodes in the Apple Podcasters Program.

#### Is it free to put a podcast on Apple Podcasts?

Yes. Listing a show on Apple Podcasts is free, and Substack hosts your podcast for free, with no hosting fees and no platform fees. Apple charges a fee only if you join the Apple Podcasters Program to sell subscriptions inside Apple Podcasts.

#### How long does it take for a podcast to appear on Apple Podcasts?

Apple doesn't give a set review time. It emails you when your show's status changes, and its approval email links to your show. After that, new episodes can take up to 24 hours to appear.

#### Do I need to submit every episode to Apple Podcasts?

No. Submit your RSS feed once. After that, every episode you publish on Substack goes to your feed, and Apple Podcasts picks it up automatically.

#### Why won't Apple Podcasts accept my RSS feed?

Your Substack feed is accepted only after you publish at least one episode, so publish an episode or a short trailer first. Also check that your cover art is square, between 1400 × 1400 and 3000 × 3000 pixels, and a JPEG or PNG.

#### Can paid subscribers listen on Apple Podcasts?

Yes. Each Substack paid subscriber gets a private RSS feed containing your paid episodes. They add it in Apple Podcasts with **Add a Show by URL**, and you keep 90% of what you earn, minus credit card fees.

Substack can also connect your podcast to Spotify and send every episode to your subscribers' inboxes.

Every part of a podcast has a free option:

On Substack, publishing is free no matter how many subscribers you have. Setting up a podcast takes one step, requires no credit card, and creates your show and its RSS feed for free.

## Podcast cover art: examples, sizes, and templates

Source: https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/cover-art

**Quick answer:** Podcast cover art must be a square image between **1400 × 1400 and 3000 × 3000 pixels**, saved as a JPEG or PNG in RGB color. Export at **3000 × 3000 pixels** so one file works on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other podcast apps.

Last updated: October 22, 2026. By [Linda Lebrun](https://substack.com/@linda), Substack.

### What makes effective podcast cover art?

Effective cover art is recognizable as a small square on a phone screen, surrounded by other shows’ covers.

[Open Tab](https://on.substack.com/s/open-tab), Substack’s interview show with media founders, demonstrates this: its title remains readable when the cover is reduced to about the size of an app icon.

| Choice | What works | What to avoid | How Open Tab does it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subject | One main image: a face, object, symbol, or the title itself | A collage of several photos | No photo; the title is the main image |
| Title | The show name in large type, occupying much of the square | Small text, long subtitles, or the word “podcast” | OPEN TAB in large lettering filling most of the square |
| Contrast | Light text on a dark or bright background, or the reverse | Text over a busy photo | Pale pink letters on a solid orange-red background |
| Identity | Colors and typefaces reusable in episode art and social posts | A style you will not keep using | The same orange-red and lettering appear on video thumbnails |

Leave “podcast” off the cover. Listeners in a podcast app already know the format, and that space is better used for a larger title.

This page is part of the [complete guide to starting a podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast). If you have not chosen a name, see [podcast name ideas](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast/podcast-names).

### Podcast cover art sizes and platform requirements

Cover art must be square, between 1400 × 1400 and 3000 × 3000 pixels, in JPEG or PNG format, RGB color, at 72 dpi. Apple Podcasts sets these requirements; artwork meeting them also works on Spotify and other podcast apps.

Open Tab uses a 2000 × 2000 pixel PNG, within Apple’s range. The same artwork appears on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and Substack.

| Artwork | Size | Shape | Format | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Show cover — required | 1400 × 1400 to 3000 × 3000 px; export at 3000 × 3000 | Square, 1:1 | JPEG or PNG, RGB, 72 dpi | Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, YouTube, and other apps |
| Episode art — optional | Same as show cover | Square, 1:1 | JPEG or PNG | Episode pages in apps that support it |
| Video thumbnail — for video podcasts | 1920 × 1080 px | Widescreen, 16:9 | JPEG or PNG | YouTube and other video platforms |
| Apple Podcasts extra artwork — optional | Varies; see Apple’s specifications | Varies | Varies | Full-page show art, chapter art, and wide artwork if submitting a show for featuring |
