### Common questions

#### How much does it cost to host a podcast on Substack?

Hosting is free, with no monthly hosting fees. When paid subscriptions are enabled, Substack takes 10% and creators keep 90%, before standard Stripe payment processing fees.

#### Is Substack good for podcasts?

The page says yes, citing its combination of a subscriber community, companion newsletter, independent website, audience ownership, free hosting, IAB-certified download analytics, and distribution to Apple Podcasts—including video—Spotify, and YouTube. It also says more than half of new subscribers come from within Substack's network.

#### Can I distribute to Apple Podcasts and Spotify?

Yes. Episodes have an RSS feed for distribution to major podcast players, including Apple Podcasts and Spotify. The FAQ describes distribution as automatic; the RSS guidance below notes that feeds can be submitted to podcast apps.

[Distribution guide](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038462911-How-do-I-distribute-my-podcast-to-apps).

#### Does my Substack podcast get an RSS feed?

Yes. Every podcast gets a free public RSS feed that can be submitted to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other apps. Each paid subscriber also gets a private RSS feed for paid episodes. Each show within a publication can have its own feed.

[RSS feeds and paid-only content](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041722272-Will-my-Podcast-RSS-feed-show-paid-only-content).

#### If I publish a video podcast on Substack, does it show up on other platforms?

Yes. Substack delivers video episodes to Apple Podcasts and can publish them automatically to YouTube. Video can also be added to Spotify through Spotify for Creators.

[Spotify video guide](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/54230275514004-How-can-I-sync-my-video-episodes-to-Spotify).

#### Can paid subscribers listen in Spotify and Apple Podcasts?

Yes. As a Spotify Open Access partner, Substack lets paid subscribers link their subscriptions and listen to paid episodes in Spotify. Private subscriber RSS feeds also work in Apple Podcasts and other podcast apps.

[Distribute paid podcasts on Spotify](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/24766453298324-How-can-I-distribute-my-paid-Substack-podcast-on-Spotify).

#### Are Substack podcast analytics IAB certified?

Yes. The page says Substack's podcast download analytics are certified by IAB Tech Lab, a measurement standard used by advertisers, allowing creators to share download numbers with sponsors.

#### Will I keep my listeners' email addresses?

Yes. Creators own their subscriber lists and can export them at any time.

#### Can I offer some episodes for free and others for paid subscribers only?

Yes. Creators control which episodes are public and which are restricted to paying subscribers. The flexible paywall supports free previews.

[Free versions and previews of paid episodes](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/8772155158164-How-do-I-create-a-free-version-of-a-paid-podcast-episode-for-free-listeners).

#### Do I need special equipment to record?

No. Substack Recording Studio works in a browser and supports recording and publishing without external software, gear, or editing tools.

#### Can I import my existing podcast?

Yes. The page says the import tool brings previous episodes, RSS feeds, and subscriber lists over in minutes.

[Podcast migration guide](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037830571-How-do-I-move-my-podcast-to-Substack).

### Substack vs Acast for podcasters

By [Zach Taylor](https://substack.com/@zach1taylor). Last updated October 21, 2026.

Acast is a podcast hosting platform built around selling ads. Its free plan stops at 5 episodes, its terms allow a paywall only through Acast or its partners, and it closed its own subscriptions product. Substack presents itself as an audience-focused alternative, with free hosting, direct paid subscriptions, and a community you own.

Substack describes itself as the only podcast hosting platform with a subscriber community, companion newsletter, independent website, growth network, and complete ownership of your audience, all built in for free. Payments run through your own Stripe account. You keep 90% of paid subscription revenue, less credit card processing fees.

### Which is better for podcasts, Substack or Acast?

The page recommends Substack for podcasters who want to earn directly from listeners rather than just from ads. Unlike Acast, Substack includes an independent website, companion newsletter, community chat, and access to every subscriber’s email address.

The page states that Substack has 21 of the 21 features in its comparison and Acast has 9, counting features with plan limits or conditions. The detailed tables below reproduce the page’s individual comparison rows.

Key differences:

- **Free hosting:** Acast’s free Starter plan is limited to 5 episodes. To keep publishing for free, you must qualify for and accept Acast’s marketplace ads. Substack has no episode cap.
- **Paid subscriptions:** Acast closed its own subscriptions product and restricts paywalls to Acast or its designated partners. Substack has built-in subscriptions and takes 10% of subscription revenue, before credit card processing fees.
- **Community:** Acast has no comments, chat, or newsletter. Substack includes chat, threaded comments, direct messages, and a newsletter.
- **Apple Podcasts video:** Acast requires its Video plan, starting at $50 per month. Substack includes it for free.

### Why podcasters choose Substack over Acast

#### Earn from listeners, and keep 90%

Acast closed Acast+, its own subscriptions product, and points creators to Supercast, which charges per subscriber. Acast’s terms allow a paywall only through Acast or its designated partners.

Substack’s paid subscriptions are built in, with payments through your own Stripe account. Substack is free to use and takes 10% of paid subscriptions, leaving creators 90% before credit card processing fees. In exchange, Substack provides a growth network intended to bring new paying subscribers, including a podcast tab in its app.

#### A growth network for your show

Acast helps advertisers find audiences but has no listener app or discovery network of its own. The page suggests pairing an Acast show with a growth network such as Substack or YouTube.

On Substack, more than half of new subscribers come from inside the network through the app, Notes, and recommendations from other publications. Shows can still go to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube.

#### Community, newsletter, and website in one place

Acast has no comments, chat, or newsletter. Its free-plan website lives on shows.acast.com and cannot be customized.

Every Substack show gets chat, threaded comments, direct messages, its own website, a newsletter, and email delivery of each episode.

#### Own your audience

According to the page, Acast’s terms give it exclusive rights to host, distribute, and monetize your show, and its help center says you cannot upload a video version of your podcast to Spotify yourself.

On Substack, payments run through your own Stripe account, and you can export your full list of free and paid subscribers at any time.

#### Hosting, video, and analytics

Both platforms have IAB-certified download analytics. Acast puts Apple Podcasts video on a plan starting at $50 per month. Substack hosts audio and video for free, automatically delivers video to Apple Podcasts, publishes it to YouTube, and includes a browser recording studio.

YouTube ends memberships 120 days after a channel loses monetization. On Substack, payments run through the creator’s own Stripe account, and the full free and paid subscriber list can be exported at any time.

## Switch to Substack

Source: https://substack.com/switch

### Move your publication to Substack

Substack presents itself as a simple way to start a subscription publication and grow it. It supports imports from Mailchimp, Beehiiv, Ghost, WordPress, TinyLetter, Medium, Tumblr, and even some custom web pages.

### Switching takes less than 5 minutes

You can import mailing lists and writing archives from the supported platforms. The page also says importing email lists, writing, and podcast episodes takes 5 minutes.

[Get help finding your import URL](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037830351).

### True independence

Own all your content and your subscriber list, build a community, and keep 90% of the revenue.

### Subscription publishing made simple

Choose which posts are free and which are available only to paid subscribers. No technical knowledge is required; Substack says it handles everything except the writing itself.

### Experiences from writers

> “After only a few months on Substack, we have multiple times more subscribers than we ever had during our time on Patreon, and we can see there's still lots of room for growth.”
>
> — Berny Belvedere, [Arc Digital](https://www.arcdigital.media/)

> “[My Substack] is already giving me more direct contact with readers than I've had in any other setting.”
>
> — Ted Gioia, [Culture Notes of an Honest Broker](https://tedgioia.substack.com/)

### Writers who have moved to Substack

The page highlights writers covering subjects from food and faith to politics and economics.

- **[Delia Cai of Deez Links](https://deezlinks.substack.com/):** Started Deez Links on TinyLetter in 2016. After moving to Substack in 2018, she experienced an “amazing growth trajectory” and joined Vanity Fair as a senior correspondent.
- **[Judd Legum of Popular Information](https://popular.info/):** The founder of political blog ThinkProgress launched Popular Information on Substack in July 2018. The page reports more than 100,000 signups.
- **[Erin Moon of The Swipe Up](https://erinhmoon.substack.com/):** Started her newsletter on Mailchimp but became frustrated by the limited interaction with readers. After moving to Substack, the page reports more than 8,500 subscribers and an approximately 50% open rate.
- **[Jarrett Carter of HBCU Digest](https://www.hbcudigest.com/):** Moved his writing to Substack after 10 years of blogging and sharing articles on social media. In one year, he built an email list of 50,000 readers.
- **[Courtney Martin of the Examined Family](https://courtney.substack.com/):** Had a weekly column at the On Being Project and transferred her readers to Substack in 2019. She was “amazed at the response” from readers eager to fund her.
- **[Jenny Rosenstrach of Dinner](https://dinneralovestory.substack.com/):** Had written Dinner: A Love Story for more than a decade. She moved her blog and its 1,500-post archive to Substack in January 2021.

> “[On Substack], I don’t need to write SEO-friendly headlines or stress about traffic numbers. I don’t have to worry about putting celebrities in my story or hoping some dubious aggregator picks up a piece. I merely have to write and hit ‘send.’ It’s a nice life.”
>
> — Ross Barkan, [Political Currents](https://rossbarkan.substack.com/)

### Compare platforms

See [how Substack compares to beehiiv](https://substack.com/substack-vs-beehiiv).

## Video creators on Substack

Source: https://substack.com/tiktok

### The new home for TikTok creators

Own your audience and earn money with subscriptions.

### Explore top creators on Substack

- **[Another New Thing with Kareem Rahma](https://substack.com/@kareemrahma)** — Comedian, writer, and producer Kareem Rahma tries new things, including “Dad Stuff™.” Also seen on @subwaytakes and @keepthemeterrunning.
- **[Miranda July](https://substack.com/@mirandajuly)** — Off-the-cuff writing, videos, pictures, and audio for paid subscribers, plus an ongoing All Fours Group Chat for everyone—not a book club, but a place to talk about your own life.
- **[Violet’s Substack](https://substack.com/@leftoversclub)** — Violet Witchel shares recipes, meal plans, shopping lists, and more for food inspiration and organization.
- **[Nothing But Respect](https://nothingbutrespect.substack.com/)** — Described as “the last uncompromised basketball podcast,” hosted by Patrick Redford and Harry Krinsky.
- **[The New Garde with Alyssa Vingan](https://substack.com/@alyssavingan)** — A podcast about the future of the fashion and beauty industries and the culture surrounding them, hosted by two-time former editor-in-chief Alyssa Vingan.
- **[Leo Skepi](https://substack.com/@leoskepi)** — Introduced with: “Let's get into it 😏 No more community guidelines & bullshit restrictions.”
- **[the sunday stack](https://sundaystack.substack.com/)** — Katie shares food she is cooking, techniques she is finding, tasty things she is trying, and other material.
- **[The Parnas Perspective](https://substack.com/@aaronparnas)** — Aaron Parnas provides a Gen Z perspective on issues in the news.
- **[FactsHQ](https://substack.com/@lisaremillard)** — “The News Girl” Lisa Remillard offers a daily dose of news, described as facts broken down simply, with no opinions.
- **[Feed Me](https://substack.com/@emilysundberg)** — Emily Sundberg’s daily newsletter about the spirit of enterprise.
- **[Throwing Fits](https://www.throwingfits.com/)** — Described as the number-one global men’s fashion and lifestyle podcast and “The Only Podcast That Matters™ (self-proclaimed).”
- **[HRH COLLECTION](https://substack.com/@hrhcollection)** — HRH’s offering, described as “UNFILTERED HRH.”
- **[Lennnie](https://substack.com/@itslennnie)** — A little blob trying to help readers get through the day.
- **[Tineke's Substack](https://substack.com/@tiniyounger)** — Tini Younger, a social media chef and influencer, contestant on *Next Level Chef* Season 2, and star of *From Scratch with Tini* on YouTube’s Bite Originals.
- **[Coco Mocoe](https://substack.com/@cocomocoe)** — A place to talk about trends, marketing, and pop culture.

### A powerful toolkit for video creators

#### Live video

Engage with your audience in real time and collaborate with other creators to leverage the Substack network.

#### Paid memberships

#### Chat

#### Discovery

### Get the app

Substack is available for [iOS](https://substack.com/app/get-ios) and [Android](https://substack.com/app/get-android).

## Video

Source: https://substack.com/video

### The home for great video

A place for creative freedom, direct connections, and a business built on subscriptions.

### Explore great videos on Substack

- **[America This Week](https://www.racket.news/s/america-this-week) — Matt Taibbi:** A national news wrap-up with Matt Taibbi and Walter Kirn, described as “so true, we recommend you stow all sharp objects before reading.”
- **[Currently Workshopping](https://cecexie.substack.com/podcast) — Cece Xie:** Part extremely online investigation and part niche liberal arts discussion, exploring ourselves, society, and the ties that bind us.
- **[Newcomer](https://www.newcomer.co/s/pod) — Newcomer:** Hosts Eric Newcomer, Max Child, and James Wilsterman present a six-part podcast series on the rise of generative artificial intelligence.
- **[House Inhabit](https://jessicareedkraus.substack.com/podcast) — Jessica Reed Kraus:** Pop culture deep dives, conspiracy theories, lifestyle highlights, and trending gossip.
- **[The Coffee Klatch](https://robertreich.substack.com/podcast) — Robert Reich:** The former Labor Secretary explores where power lies in the system and how it is used and abused.
- **[The Chris Hedges Report](https://chrishedges.substack.com/podcast) — Chris Hedges:** Coverage of US foreign policy, economic realities, and civil liberties in American society.
- **[Decoding the News](https://www.offmessage.net/podcast) — Brian Buetler:** Why mainstream political media so often misses the mark, and how to consume it like a news professional.
- **[JENNY SAIS QUOI](https://jennywalton.substack.com/podcast) — Jenny Walton:** “A nice little place to chat, that isn't Instagram.”
- **[Ungodly](https://shalomauslander.substack.com/s/ungodly) — Shalom Auslander:** “Good Lessons From a Bad God.”
- **[Three Ingredients](https://threeingredients.substack.com/podcast) — Ruth Reichl:** Conversations about food with Nancy Silverton, Laurie Ochoa, and Ruth Reichl.
- **[So Into That](https://whattocook.substack.com/podcast) — Caroline Chambers:** Conversations about finding easier and better ways to do—and enjoy—life.
- **[Further Ado](https://ambertamblyn.substack.com/) — Amber Tamblyn:** Exploring new creative thresholds, staying politically and spiritually engaged in difficult times, and behind-the-scenes stories from Tamblyn’s three decades in entertainment.
- **[The Chris Cuomo Project](https://thechriscuomoproject.substack.com/) — Chris Cuomo:** Politics, global affairs, and American culture, viewed through Cuomo’s years of insider experience.
- **[Dumpster Fire](https://www.phetasy.com/s/dumpster-fire-podcast) — Bridget Phetasy:** A satirical show created and hosted by comedian Bridget Phetasy, looking at the week in news, current events, and politics.
- **[The Lesbian Project](https://www.thelesbianprojectpod.com/podcast) — Julie Bindel & Kathleen Stock:** “All the sapphic traffic”—for anyone who wants more lesbian in their life.
- **[True Hoop](https://www.truehoop.com/podcast) — Jarod Hector & David Thorpe:** Award-winning hard truths about the NBA since 2005.

### A powerful toolkit for video creators

#### Video podcasts

Upload video episodes to Substack and publish automatically to YouTube, Spotify, Apple, and all other podcast listening apps. [Learn about podcasting on Substack](https://substack.com/podcasts).

The page also highlights these toolkit features:

- Paid exclusives
- Live Video
- One home for everything
- Shareable clips

### Video questions answered

#### How do I set up a video podcast?

Follow the [step-by-step guide](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/21093671091220), or read the [overview of podcasting on Substack](https://substack.com/podcasts).

If you are moving from another host, see [how Substack compares to other podcast hosts](https://substack.com/best-podcast-hosting). If you are starting a new show, read [how to start a podcast](https://substack.com/how-to-start-a-podcast).

#### How much does it cost to use Substack to host my videos and/or podcast?

It is free to publish on Substack. If you turn on paid subscriptions, you keep **90% of subscription revenue, minus credit card fees**.

#### How can subscribers watch videos published on Substack?

Subscribers get new videos directly in their inbox. They can click through to watch on the web or in [the Substack app](https://substack.com/app?no_redirect=true).

#### Will Substack help me grow my audience?

Substack describes audience growth as one of the main benefits of publishing on its platform. According to the page, [more than 50% of all new free subscriptions and around 25% of paid subscriptions](https://on.substack.com/p/substack-generates-1-in-3-new-subscriptions) to Substack publications come from within its network.

#### What if my question or problem is not answered here?

Find answers to frequently asked questions in the [Support center](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us), or [search for more help](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&query=video).
